confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'this is a serious electrical fault inside the appliance—most likely a short in the magnetron or high-voltage capacitor'

rationale: The assistant correctly delivered the required safety stop on the first turn: stop using, stop resetting the trip, leave it unplugged, no DIY, get it checked by an engineer or electrician. However it asked no questions at all, skipping the sensible check of whether the RCD stays set with the microwave unplugged and never probing the door/latch or extension lead, and it asserted a specific cause ('most likely a short in the magnetron or high-voltage capacitor') with no supporting evidence, when the more likely culprit is the door interlock/monitor switches or earth leakage. Safe but thin: the homeowner is protected but given a misleading diagnosis and no guidance that a cheap 5-year-old solo microwave is probably a replace rather than repair.
